label: copy phase after the first output (steps t > L)
explanation: Dense copy-phase feature. It fires on about 95% of copy-phase steps (t > L, recall_idx >= 1) for every output position and every token, and these steps hold 99.5% of its activation mass. It is essentially silent on the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0) and on original-phase steps t >= 1. The only exception is a weak, low-magnitude firing at t = 0 in about 23% of sequences (0.5% of mass). Token identity (in_tok, out_tok, prev_tok, first_tok), L, digit count and repeats barely change the firing rate. Magnitude varies a lot between sequences, and the top examples peak somewhere in the middle of the copy phase, but no simple variable that explains magnitude was found. The misses are mostly low-quartile activations at t = 0.

issues: Minor: the t=0 firing is token-dependent. (t==0)&isin(in_tok,[p,r,c]) has precision 1.0, but it covers only 1.8% of active steps and 0.2% of mass. The explanation already notes the weak t=0 firing, and the size is negligible.

The 5% of copy steps where it is silent look like scattered noise. Precision stays between 0.93 and 0.98 across every slice tested: recall_idx<=2 (0.933), recall_idx>2 (0.960), recall_idx==1 with L<=4 (0.983) or L>=8 (0.946), to_go==0 (0.943), digit inputs (0.946), in_tok==first_tok (0.937), out_count>1 (0.949) and in_count>1 (0.949). On the test split, 82.7% of the bottom activation quartile is covered and essentially 100% of the upper quartiles.

Every factual claim checks out on the test split. phase==2 gives precision 0.950, recall 0.957, F1 0.954 and mass recall 0.995. The <DEL> step has 15 activations out of 500k. Original-phase steps t>=1 are essentially silent. t=0 fires in 23.2% of sequences and holds 0.5% of mass. The variable 'correct' adds nothing because nearly all copy steps are correct.
